subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Santos <elena.santos@acmepay.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel@acmepay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria

Hi Elena / Miguel,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to put a short recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we’re aligned on success criteria, timeline, and who owns what.

Summary of need
- Goal: Improve multilingual customer support triage and routing across English, Spanish, and Portuguese.
- Volume: ~20k messages/month; peak concurrency low but P95 latency matters for UX.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks)
1) Inference trial with 2 model variants: primary open model + fallback smaller model for cost/latency tradeoff.
2) Evaluation: intent accuracy, entity extraction, hallucination checks, and runtime metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec).
3) Integration: sample batch of 2k recent support transcripts from Acme (anonymized) + 200 live-simulated messages.

Suggested success criteria
- Intent classification F1 >= 0.90 across EN/ES/PT
- Entity extraction F1 >= 0.85
- Hallucination / wrong-answer rate < 5% on sampled checks
- P95 latency <= 300ms (in our hosted Redwood environment)
- Cost: expected inference cost per 1M tokens <= budget threshold (we’ll provide estimates)

Model recommendation (initial)
- Primary: Llama-3-13B (quantized) — good balance of multilingual capability and generation quality for structured extraction tasks.
- Fallback: Mistral-Instruct-7B (or another smaller 7B variant) — lower latency/cost for heavier throughput paths; degrade gracefully.

Ownership & next steps
- Acme: provide anonymized transcript sample + PO for trial access (procurement contact: {please confirm}).
- Redwood: provision test endpoint, baseline eval harness, and initial model config (Marissa / Jordan).
- Timeline: kickoff this week, data upload by Mon 6/29, baseline results by Fri 7/10.

Attached: redwood-poc-template.pdf (POC plan + eval template).

If that looks good, can we lock the kickoff time for Tues 6/30 at 10am PT?

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & success criteria

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. Quick clarifications:
- Multilingual: Spanish and Portuguese are critical for our LATAM customers; we have about 30% Spanish, 10% Portuguese traffic.
- Data: We can provide a 2k anonymized transcript batch by Mon 6/29. I will confirm with procurement on a short PO for the trial credits.
- Latency target: P95 <= 300ms is acceptable; can we also capture cold-start / first-token times?

On models — Llama-3-13B looks promising. A couple of asks:
1) Can you include a fallback model that is cheaper but still handles Spanish reasonably well?
2) We’d like to see an initial quality comparison on a 200-message validation set across EN/ES/PT.

Happy to take the Tues 6/30 10am PT slot if Jordan can join to discuss integration details.

Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Santos <elena.santos@acmepay.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel@acmepay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & success criteria

Elena — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups inline and an updated plan: 

- Cold-start: yes, we’ll capture first-token latency and warm/cold differences in the baseline report.
- Fallback model: we’ll use Mistral-Instruct-7B as the fallback; it has reasonable multilingual behavior and much lower inference cost.
- Validation set: please send the 200-message set (EN/ES/PT split) as a CSV with columns: id, language, text, expected_intent (optional).

Updated timeline (concrete)
- Mon 6/29: Acme uploads anonymized transcripts + validation set, procurement confirms short PO.
- Tue 6/30 10:00 PT: Kickoff call (Jordan will review integration + endpoint config).
- Wed 7/1 - Thu 7/9: Run baseline evals, collect metrics across models.
- Fri 7/10: Deliver evaluation report and recommendations.

Evaluation plan (deliverables)
- Per-language intent F1 and entity F1 (EN/ES/PT)
- Hallucination sampling report (10 random checks per language)
- Runtime metrics: P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, memory usage (approx)
- Cost projection for 1M tokens for each model variant

Technical notes for integration (Jordan)
- We’ll provide a short SDK and a prebuilt eval harness; Jordan will share the exact API call shapes.
- Data security: Rishi — we’ll need to confirm retention and access controls for the uploaded data; will use customer-scoped storage and delete after the trial unless otherwise requested.

Attached: poc-tech-specs.docx (integration checklist + API examples).

If all good I’ll get the endpoint provisioned today so we can get results early next week.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Hi all,

Quick engineering notes ahead of the kickoff:
- Baseline infra: we’ll spin up a small dedicated sandbox endpoint in Redwood hosted mode with the Llama-3-13B quantized profile and a second endpoint for Mistral-Instruct-7B.
- Latency expectations: on our infra we expect P95 ~200-350ms for Llama-3-13B depending on sequence length; Mistral-7B should be closer to 120-250ms. We’ll report exact values per your 200-msg validation set.
- Throughput: batching will be enabled but kept conservative to meet P95 SLO. We’ll provide the batch config used in the report so you can reproduce.
- Fallback routing: if Llama-3-13B exceeds a 350ms threshold or OOMs, requests will route to Mistral-7B with a tagged response indicating fallback.
- Evaluation harness: we’ll run intent/entity extraction via a structured output prompt and compute F1. For hallucination checks we’ll use automated heuristics + manual sampling.

Looking forward to the kickoff Tues at 10am PT. I’ll bring the API examples and sample eval scripts.

– Jordan
Principal Services Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
